q: Project A has an NPV of 120,000 over 5 years; Project B has an NPV of 95,000 over 3 years. Based only on NPV, which project should be selected?
o: Project A, because it has the higher NPV
Project B, because it is shorter
Project B, because NPV should be divided by the number of years
Neither, because NPV cannot compare projects
e: NPV already accounts for the time value of money over the life of each project, so the number of years is not used again. Select the project with the higher NPV.

q: An investment of 300,000 produces net cash inflows of 75,000 per year. What is the simple payback period?
o: 4 years
3 years
5 years
2.5 years
e: Payback period = initial investment / annual inflow = 300,000 / 75,000 = 4 years (ignoring the time value of money).

q: A project has a benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 0.8. What does this mean?
o: Costs exceed benefits; the project is not financially attractive
Benefits exceed costs by 80%
The project will pay back in 0.8 years
The project's internal rate of return is 80%
e: BCR = benefits / costs. A ratio below 1.0 means costs are greater than benefits.

q: The organization chose Project X (NPV 250,000) over Project Y (NPV 180,000). What is the opportunity cost of choosing Project X?
e: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative not chosen, i.e., the NPV of Project Y: 180,000.

q: Halfway through, a project has spent 2 million. A new analysis shows that completing it will cost 3 million more and deliver benefits of 2.5 million. A manager argues they must continue because 2 million has already been spent. What is the flaw in this reasoning?
o: The 2 million is a sunk cost and should not influence the decision
The analysis should add the 2 million to the expected benefits
Projects should never be stopped once started
The benefits must be discounted by the 2 million
e: Sunk costs are already spent and cannot be recovered; decisions should be based on future costs and benefits. Here the remaining 3 million cost exceeds the 2.5 million benefit.

q: When comparing two projects, which one is generally preferred according to IRR?
o: The project with the higher IRR
The project with the lower IRR
The project whose IRR equals the inflation rate
IRR cannot be used to compare projects
e: The internal rate of return is the discount rate at which NPV equals zero. A higher IRR indicates a more attractive return, all else being equal.

q: The finance department asks the project manager to classify project costs as capital or operating expenditure. Why does this matter?
o: CapEx and OpEx are treated differently in financial reporting and taxation
Only OpEx can be included in the cost baseline
CapEx is always funded from management reserve
It determines the critical path
e: Capital expenditures (creating long-term assets) are capitalized and depreciated, while operating expenditures are expensed in the period. The classification affects financial statements, funding sources and approvals.

q: An agile team of 8 people has a fully loaded cost of 60,000 per two-week sprint. The release is forecast at 6 sprints. What is the forecast labor cost for the release?
e: With a stable team, agile cost forecasting is often based on team run rate: 60,000 per sprint × 6 sprints = 360,000.

q: In many adaptive projects, the team and timebox are fixed while scope is variable. How does this affect financial management?
o: Cost is relatively predictable; the product owner maximizes value delivered within the budget
Cost cannot be estimated at all
Cost is controlled through a detailed bottom-up WBS estimate
The project must use a fixed-price contract for every feature
e: With fixed teams and cadence, costs are largely known per iteration. Financial control focuses on maximizing value by prioritizing the backlog within the available funding.

q: Leadership wants to fund an innovative product incrementally, releasing money based on demonstrated results. Which approach BEST fits?
o: Incremental (stage-based) funding tied to validated outcomes
A single fixed budget approved at initiation
Funding only after the full product is delivered
Funding based on the number of team members
e: Incremental funding reduces financial risk on uncertain initiatives by releasing funds in stages based on evidence (e.g., MVP results, achieved milestones), aligning finance with value delivery.

q: Which of the following is a cost of conformance?
o: Training staff and testing products before release
Rework of defective products
Warranty claims
Lost business due to poor reputation
e: Cost of conformance includes prevention costs (training, documentation, equipment) and appraisal costs (testing, inspection). Rework, warranty claims and lost business are costs of nonconformance (failure costs).

q: A project manager is choosing between two pieces of equipment. One is cheaper to buy, but the other uses far less energy and lasts twice as long. Which concept should guide the decision?
o: Life-cycle costing
Sunk cost
Analogous estimating
Crashing
e: Life-cycle costing considers the total cost of ownership over the life of an asset (acquisition, operation, maintenance, disposal), supporting value-based and sustainable decisions.

q: Which document defines how benefits will be measured, who is accountable and when they are expected to be realized?
o: Benefits management plan
Cost management plan
Procurement management plan
Requirements traceability matrix
e: The benefits management plan describes target benefits, metrics, the timeframe for realization, the benefits owner and how benefits will be sustained after the project.

q: Midway through a project, the CPI is 0.95 and the SPI is 1.05. The sponsor asks whether the project will finish within budget. What is the BEST response?
o: Calculate EAC and present the forecast together with options to improve cost performance
Confirm it will finish on budget because SPI is above 1.0
Tell the sponsor it is too early to forecast
Request management reserve immediately
e: A CPI below 1.0 signals a cost overrun trend. The project manager should forecast EAC/VAC, explain causes and propose corrective options, rather than relying on schedule performance.

q: Which statement about the cost baseline is TRUE?
o: It excludes management reserve and is changed only through formal change control
It includes management reserve
It can be updated by the project manager whenever costs change
It is the same as the funding requirement in every period
e: The cost baseline is the approved, time-phased budget excluding management reserve. Changes require formal change control. Funding requirements may include management reserve and are often released in increments.

q: A team is tracking an agile release using cost per story point. 40% of the release points are complete and 45% of the release budget has been spent. What does this suggest?
o: Spending is running ahead of value delivered, signaling a potential cost overrun
The release is under budget
The release is ahead of schedule
No conclusion can be drawn in agile projects
e: Comparing percent of work complete (value earned) with percent of budget spent is the agile equivalent of CPI: 0.40 / 0.45 ≈ 0.89, indicating cost performance below plan.

q: A project manager presents a financial forecast showing that, at the current spending rate, the project will need additional funding in Q3. When should this be raised to the sponsor?
o: As soon as the forecast indicates the need, so options can be considered early
Only after the money has run out
At project closure in the final report
Only if the CPI falls below 0.5
e: Transparent and early communication of financial forecasts gives governance bodies time to decide on corrective actions, re-prioritization or additional funding.
